about.title: Livermore Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Livermore's workday stretches across warehouses, construction sites, vineyards, delivery routes and offices, and a serious injury in any of them can upend a household fast. If you were hurt while working in Livermore, California's workers' compensation system is normally your route to medical care and partial wage replacement from your employer, and it applies whether or not anyone was at fault. That system, though, is usually the exclusive remedy against the employer itself. Many people don't realize a second path may exist: when a subcontractor, a property owner, the maker of a defective tool, or another driver on I-580 or Isabel Avenue caused the harm, a separate third-party injury claim can be considered alongside the comp case. Two rules matter early. Report the injury to your employer within 30 days, and know that the third-party claim carries a two-year deadline. Retaliation for reporting is illegal. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm; we connect Alameda County workers with an independent attorney who can sort out which claims fit your situation.

items.question: I was rear-ended on I-580 while making deliveries for my Livermore employer. Is that just a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were on the job, workers' compensation would typically cover your medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of fault. The other driver, however, is a third party, so a separate injury claim against them may also be possible. Livermore recorded 364 injury collisions in 2025, with reported crashes peaking on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., so on-duty drivers in this area do face this situation.

items.question: What happens if I wait too long to tell my employer I got hurt?
items.answer: California asks you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days. Waiting past that can complicate or weaken your workers' compensation claim, even if the injury is real. If the injury developed gradually, report it as soon as you connect it to your work. An attorney can explain how the timing rules apply to your facts.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a claim after an injury in Livermore?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' compensation claim is illegal in California. That includes firing, demoting, cutting hours or threatening you because you spoke up. If you believe this has happened, the attorney you are connected with can review whether you have additional claims beyond the injury itself.
